The given equation \(\frac{1}{x} + 5x^2 = 6x - 24\) can be transformed into a standard polynomial form. To do this, first eliminate the fraction by multiplying every term by \(x\):

\[ x \left( \frac{1}{x} + 5x^2 \right) = x (6x - 24) \]

This simplifies to:

\[ 1 + 5x^3 = 6x^2 - 24x \]

Rearrange all terms to one side of the equation to get it into standard polynomial form:

\[ 5x^3 - 6x^2 - 24x + 1 = 0 \]

This is a cubic polynomial equation. The roots \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) of this polynomial are the values that satisfy the equation when substituted for \(x\). According to Vieta's formulas, the sum of the roots \(a + b + c\) of the polynomial \(5x^3 - 6x^2 - 24x + 1 = 0\) can be found using the coefficient of \(x^2\):

\[ a + b + c = -\frac{\text{coefficient of } x^2}{\text{leading coefficient}} = -\left( \frac{-6}{5} \right) = \frac{6}{5} \]

Thus, the sum of the roots \(a + b + c\) is \(\frac{6}{5}\).
